correctness.rationale: For an affine pencil P_n of n>=2 distinct complex lines, the anti-admissibility condition for a surjection H1(complement)=Z^n to F_p^k reduces exactly to g_i spanning and each pair (g_i, S=sum g_j) linearly independent at the single singular point. For k=2,p=2, all admissible g_i must be the two nonzero vectors away from span(S), and their multiplicities must both be odd; hence n even is necessary and sufficient. For any odd p, assign r=1 meridians e1 and the rest e2 unless n congruent1 modulo p, in which case r=2; both coefficients of S then nonzero. For k>=3, assign e1..ek once, repeat e1 for excess meridians; S has e2 and e3 components 1 and is never proportional to any image. All maps are onto. Thus p_A(P_n,2)=2 even n, 3 odd n; all 3<=k<=n have threshold 2. It concerns affine (not projective) pencils, elementary abelian targets, and primes, with all quantifiers addressed.
